He played [[college basketball]] for [[Northwest Florida State College|Northwest Florida State]] and [[Morehead State Eagles men's basketball|Morehead State]]. The nephew of former [[National Basketball Association|NBA]] basketball player [[Jamario Moon]],{{cite web|first=Sabreena|last=Merchant|title=Clippings: The Moonshot Has Finally Landed|url=https://www.clipsnation.com/2022/1/4/22866149/la-clippers-news-xavier-moon-10-day-contract-moonshot-brian-shaw|website=ClipsNation.com|date=January 4, 2022|access-date=January 14, 2022|archive-date=January 14, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220114044912/https://www.clipsnation.com/2022/1/4/22866149/la-clippers-news-xavier-moon-10-day-contract-moonshot-brian-shaw|url-status=dead}} he won [[CEBL Player of the Year]] three years in a row from 2019 to 2021 while playing for the [[Edmonton Stingers]]. ==High school career== Moon grew up in [[Goodwater, Alabama]] and began playing organized basketball in seventh grade. He attended [[Coosa County School District|Central Coosa High School]] where he played on the junior varsity team as a freshman before playing three years on varsity.{{cite web |last1=Maloney |first1=Mark |title=FAMILY AND DETERMINATION HAVE HELPED XAVIER MOON PERSEVERE THROUGH ADVERSITY |url=https://msueagles.com/news/2016/12/10/mens-basketball-family-helps-xavier-moon-persevere-through-adversity.aspx |website=[[Morehead State Eagles]] |access-date=July 1, 2020 |date=December 20, 2016}} As a senior, he led Alabama in scoring with 35 points per game. In the tournament semifinal, he scored 48 points, followed by 50 points in the championship game. Moon earned Alabama Sports Writers Association All-State team honors and went to the Alabama-Mississippi All-Star game.{{cite news |last1=Arbogast |first1=Lizi |title=Central Coosa's Xavier Moon signs pro contract to play in France |url=https://www.alexcityoutlook.com/sports/centralcoosa/central-coosa-s-xavier-moon-signs-pro-contract-to-play-in-france/article_d6ef0b45-4f4b-5d1b-a472-bad10b368701.html |access-date=July 1, 2020 |work=Alexander City Outlook |date=August 10, 2017}} Moon also played on the football team as a senior as a quarterback. He was lightly recruited, as [[Itawamba Community College]] was the first school to offer him a scholarship during his senior season, and Moon ended up signing with [[Northwest Florida State College]]. ==College career== Moon attended [[Northwest Florida State College]] for two years. As a freshman, he averaged 4.6 points per game. He averaged 7.7 points per game as a sophomore. Moon was named Sixth Man of the Year as the Raiders finished 33-2 and won the National Junior College Championship. Moon transferred to [[Morehead State Eagles men's basketball|Morehead State]] before his junior season, choosing the Eagles because it felt like home. He finished second on the team in scoring as a junior at 10.2 points per game and shot 48 percent from the field. Moon recorded the first [[triple-double]] in Morehead State history on December 19, 2016, notching 25 points, 11 assists and 10 rebounds against [[Central Arkansas Bears men's basketball|Central Arkansas]]. He scored a career-high 26 points against [[Austin Peay Governors men's basketball|Austin Peay]] on January 19, 2017. As a senior, Moon led Morehead State in scoring with 16.0 points per game and also averaged 4.6 assists and 3.5 rebounds per game. He was named to the First Team All-[[Ohio Valley Conference]]. Moon graduated from Morehead State in May 2017 with a bachelor's degree in Exercise Science.{{cite web |last1=Lambert |first1=Tyler |title=EAGLE ALUM XAVIER MOON HEADING TO NBA G-LEAGUE |url=https://msueagles.com/news/2019/10/17/mens-basketball-eagle-alum-xavier-moon-heading-to-nba-g-league.aspx |website=[[Morehead State Eagles]] |access-date=July 1, 2020 |date=October 17, 2019}} ==Professional career== ===ALM Évreux (2017–2018)=== On August 10, 2017, Moon signed his first professional contract with [[ALM Évreux Basket]] of the [[LNB Pro B]]. After six months, Moon left the team due to issues with the coach and returned home to Alabama. ===Albany Patroons (2018)=== His uncle [[Jamario Moon]] suggested that he join his team, the [[Albany Patroons]], and Xavier did so after coach [[Derrick Rowland]] was impressed with his play. In the Patroon locker room, Xavier became known as "half Moon", in contrast with his uncle, known as "full Moon".{{cite news |last1=Wilkin |first1=Tim |title=2 Moons Patroons' boon |url=https://www.timesunion.com/sports/article/2-Moons-Patroons-boon-12708051.php |access-date=July 1, 2020 |work=[[Albany Times-Union]] |date=February 26, 2018}} Xavier averaged 18 points, 8 rebounds and 6 assists per game and was named [[North American Premier Basketball]] rookie of the year.{{cite journal |title=Lightning Sign Xavier Moon |url=https://lightningbasketball.ca/Moon_Signing |website=[[London Lightning]] |access-date=July 1, 2020 |date=September 7, 2018}} ===London Lightning (2018–2019)=== Moon signed with [[London Lightning]] of the [[National Basketball League of Canada]] on September 7, 2018. He averaged 13.7 points, 4.9 rebounds and 4.1 assists per game in 40 games.{{cite journal |title=Lightning Re-Sign Speed Guard Xavier Moon |url=https://www.lightningbasketball.ca/sports/mbkb/2019-20/releases/Signing_-_Moon |website=[[London Lightning]] |access-date=July 1, 2020}} ===Edmonton Stingers (2019–2020)=== [[Alex Johnson (basketball)|Alex Johnson]] informed Moon of the formation of the [[Canadian Elite Basketball League]], and he joined the [[Edmonton Stingers]]. In his first game on May 11, 2019, he scored 36 points in a 118–105 overtime victory against the [[Niagara River Lions]].{{cite news |last1=Moddejonge |first1=Gerry |title=Lunar landing: Xavier Moon blasts off in Stingers opener |url=https://edmontonsun.com/sports/basketball/lunar-landing-xavier-moon-blasts-off-in-stingers-opener |access-date=July 1, 2020 |work=[[Edmonton Sun]] |date=May 11, 2019}} Moon averaged 19.3 points and 5.7 assists per game for Edmonton and was named league MVP. He led the team to the semifinals before losing to the eventual champions [[Saskatchewan Rattlers]]. Following the season, Moon tried out for [[Raptors 905]] of the [[NBA G League]] but was one of the final roster cuts.{{cite news |last1=Van Diest |first1=Derek |title=Canadian Elite Basketball League MVP Xavier Moon excited for return to Edmonton Stingers |url=https://edmontonsun.com/sports/basketball/canadian-elite-basketball-league-mvp-xavier-moon-excited-for-return-to-edmonton-stingers |access-date=July 1, 2020 |work=[[Edmonton Sun]] |date=April 15, 2020}} ===Return to the Lightning (2019–2020)=== He re-signed with the Lightning on November 15.{{cite news |last1=Vanderhoeven 2019}} On January 4, 2020, he scored 39 points in a 113–97 victory over the [[KW Titans]].{{cite news |last1=Stubbs |first1=Mike |title=Xavier Moon's big night has London Lightning off to a 4-1 start to the season |url=https://globalnews.ca/news/6367980/nbl-of-canada-xavier-moon-london-lightning/ |access-date=July 1, 2020 |work=Global News |date=January 4, 2020}} Moon averaged 21.5 points, 6.5 rebounds and 5.3 assists per game during the shortened 2019–20 season and was named to the First Team All-NBL Canada.{{cite news |last1=Vanderhoeven |first1=Paul |title=NBLC aims for new season in December, four London Lightning players get all-star nods |url=https://lfpress.com/sports/basketball/london-lightning/nblc |access-date=July 1, 2020 |work=[[London Free Press]] |date=July 1, 2020}} On (2020)=== Moon re-joined the Edmonton Stingers for the [[2020 CEBL season]]. He scored 31 points in the championship game, a 90–73 win against the [[Fraser Valley Bandits]], and was named the Final MVP.{{cite news |last1=McGaughey |first1=Paul |title=Xavier Moon ices win for Stingers over Bandits in CEBL championship game |url=https://www.cbc.ca/sports/basketball/cebl/cebl-summer-series-championship-game-bandits-stingers-1.5679926 |access-date=August 11, 2020 |work=[[Canadian Broadcasting Corporation]] |date=August 9, 2020}} He also won his second Most Valuable Player award.{{cite web | url=https://www.cebl.ca/poty#:~:text=Niagara%20ON%3A%20The%20Canadian%20Elite,covering%20the%20CEBL%20Summer%20Series | title=Xavier Moon Wins His Second CEBL Player of the Year Award }} Moon averaged 19.5 points, 4.5 assists, 4 rebounds and 1.8 steals per game.{{cite news |last1=Moddejonge |first1=Gerry |title=Edmonton Stingers guard Xavier Moon goes two-for-two in CEBL MVP awards |url=https://edmontonsun.com/sports/basketball/edmonton-stingers-guard-xavier-moon-goes-two-for-two-in-cebl-mvp-awards |access-date=December 25, 2021 |work=[[Edmonton Sun]] |date=September 2, 2020}} ===Maccabi Hod HaSharon (2020–2021)=== In August 2020 Moon signed with [[Maccabi Hod HaSharon]] of the Israeli National League.{{Cite web|date=2021-02-01|title=Edmonton Stingers Re-Sign Xavier Moon:
